title: Humansand Open-Sources Tool to Speed Up Large-Scale RL Weight Updates
summary:
A new method developed by Humansand reduces the sampler pause time for reinforcement learning (RL) to less than 0.23 seconds. The software, known as "weight teleportation," uses GPUs to perform parallel compression of model weight updates and integrates with Nvidia's Blackwell chip architecture to allow these updates to be transmitted between clusters at internet speeds.

The system handles non-blocking compression and preparation in approximately 3 seconds, addressing a technical bottleneck that previously required training and sampling components to be located within the same data center to manage high data volumes. Humansand has released the technology as open-source to facilitate the deployment of decentralized RL across distributed hardware.

selectedTweets.bestBit: Weight teleportation is so efficient (<0.23s sampler pause time, ~3s non-blocking compression + prepare), the bottleneck ends up being the GPU hardware’s decompression ASIC
selectedTweets.text:
Large-scale RL has a problem: weight updates from trainers to samplers are slow and expensive

We’re sharing weight teleportation: faster weight updates than existing intra-cluster techniques with internet speeds, enabling samplers anywhere (maybe even space!)

Weight teleportation is so efficient (<0.23s sampler pause time, ~3s non-blocking compression + prepare), the bottleneck ends up being the GPU hardware’s decompression ASIC

We unlock these gains by using GPUs for massively parallel compression of model weight changes, engineering a heterogeneous decompression and patching pipeline, along with other optimizations and overlaps. These techniques are co-designed with hardware-native features in NVIDIA’s Blackwell generation of chips

We’ve open-sourced weight teleportation, so everyone can use it today
